faqs.q: How much does a Bohemian Shepherd cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $800–$3,000 for a Bohemian Shepherd puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Bohemian Shepherd?
faqs.a: Budget $150–$300 per month for a Bohemian Shepherd, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Mid-size breeds sit in the moderate cost range across most ownership categories.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Bohemian Shepherd?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($500–900), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($$400–$1,200 per year). Grooming costs are lower for short-coated breeds managed at home.

faqs.q: How much does a Bohemian Shepherd cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Bohemian Shepherd are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $2,000–$4,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Bohemian Shepherd?
faqs.a: Bohemian Shepherds need brushing once or twice per week.  Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Bohemian Shepherds shed a lot?
faqs.a: Bohemian Shepherds shed minimally. A weekly brush is usually sufficient.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Bohemian Shepherd need?
faqs.a: A rubber grooming glove or soft-bristle brush is sufficient for weekly maintenance on the Bohemian Shepherd's medium coat. Add a nail grinder and ear cleaner for a complete grooming kit.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Bohemian Shepherd?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Bohemian Shepherds that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Bohemian Shepherds easy to train?
faqs.a: Bohemian Shepherds are considered easier to train than average — they respond quickly to reward-based methods and generalise cues well. Short 10–15 minute sessions outperform long correction-heavy drills.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Bohemian Shepherd?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Bohemian Shepherds. Keep sessions short and positive, end on a success, and vary your rewards to maintain engagement.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Bohemian Shepherd?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Bohemian Shepherd?
faqs.a: Most Bohemian Shepherds learn basic obedience cues (sit, stay, come, down) within 2–4 weeks of daily practice. Reliable recall in distracting environments typically takes 2–3 months of consistent reinforcement.

faqs.q: What health problems do Bohemian Shepherds commonly have?
faqs.a: Bohemian Shepherds are most commonly associated with routine age-related conditions. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Bohemian Shepherds live?
faqs.a: Bohemian Shepherds have an average lifespan of 12–15 years. Good nutrition, appropriate exercise, weight management and regular vet visits are the key factors in achieving the upper end of this range.

faqs.q: Are Bohemian Shepherds prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Hip dysplasia is less common in Bohemian Shepherds than in large working breeds, but it can still occur. Responsible breeders screen breeding stock. Keeping your Bohemian Shepherd at a healthy weight is the most effective preventive measure.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Bohemian Shepherd puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Bohemian Shepherd puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Bohemian Shepherd-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Bohemian Shepherds good with kids?
faqs.a: Bohemian Shepherds are generally known for being friendly and patient, making them well-suited to family life with children. Supervision is always recommended with young children regardless of breed — interactions should be taught from both sides.

faqs.q: Do Bohemian Shepherds get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Bohemian Shepherds can be selective with other dogs due to their protective nature. Early socialisation in puppy classes and controlled on-lead introductions with other dogs help build positive associations.

faqs.q: Do Bohemian Shepherds bark a lot?
faqs.a: Bohemian Shepherds tend to be vocal — they may bark at strangers, sounds, or when under-stimulated. Adequate daily exercise and mental enrichment (training sessions, puzzle feeders) significantly reduce nuisance barking. Teaching a "quiet" cue early is worthwhile.

faqs.q: Are Bohemian Shepherds good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Bohemian Shepherds can live in apartments if their exercise needs are met consistently. The key variable is owner commitment to daily walks and enrichment — breed size alone doesn't determine apartment suitability.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Bohemian Shepherd need per day?
faqs.a: Bohemian Shepherds need approximately 45–60 minutes of exercise daily. A structured morning walk and an evening sniff walk usually cover their needs. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Bohemian Shepherds good running partners?
faqs.a: Bohemian Shepherds can join you for moderate runs once fully grown. They're better suited to steady 3–5 mile runs than extended distance. Watch for signs of fatigue and always run in cooler hours during summer.

faqs.q: What happens if a Bohemian Shepherd doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Bohemian Shepherds are less demanding than high-energy breeds, but chronic under-exercise still leads to weight gain and low-level restlessness. Even lower-energy breeds benefit from a consistent daily walk for both physical health and mental stimulation.

faqs.q: Can a Bohemian Shepherd be off-lead?
faqs.a: Off-lead freedom for a Bohemian Shepherd depends on recall reliability, not breed alone. Train recall from puppyhood using long-line sessions before progressing to full off-lead. A standard 20-foot long-line gives freedom while maintaining safety during the training phase.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Bohemian Shepherd?
faqs.a: A Bohemian Shepherd needs approximately 1½–3 cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Bohemian Shepherd?
faqs.a: Adult Bohemian Shepherds should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Bohemian Shepherd?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Medium-energy Bohemian Shepherds do well on standard adult maintenance formulas with named protein as the first ingredient.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Bohemian Shepherd from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Most Bohemian Shepherds can transition to adult food between 12 and 15 months. Transition gradually over 7–10 days — mix 25% new food with 75% old food and shift the ratio every 2 days to avoid digestive upset.

faqs.q: Is a Bohemian Shepherd a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Bohemian Shepherds are generally considered suitable for first-time owners. They're responsive to training, manageable in size, and adaptable to different home environments. A puppy class is still recommended to build a strong foundation.

faqs.q: Are Bohemian Shepherds good family dogs?
faqs.a: Bohemian Shepherds are typically affectionate family dogs that do well with children and adapt to household routines. Their sociable nature means they prefer company over isolation.

faqs.q: Do Bohemian Shepherds do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Bohemian Shepherds form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Bohemian Shepherd?
faqs.a: Plan for 1.5–2 hours per day dedicated to your Bohemian Shepherd — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction.  The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
